task_card.title: Object Stamp Flow - extract an object from one image, place it into another

next_action.description: Split js/components/Organisms/MpiStepPlace into TWO step kinds per plan.md § Plan Drift 2026-08-27 - a `cutout` kind on image2 (the object alone on a large canvas: Remove Background, Erase/Restore, UndoStack; no gizmo, so no `move` tool) and `place` on image1 keeping ShapeManager + Auto/Manual. Add `sourceValue: _stepValues[step.sourceRole]` beside the `source` prop already in _buildStepSlide, so stage 3 can render what stage 2 produced. The code is written and proven - this is a move, not a rewrite.

key_decisions: THE CLEANUP IS ITS OWN STAGE (Fabio, 2026-08-27). Cleaning the object is work on the OBJECT; placing it is work on the SCENE. One combined stage forced the brush to be Auto-only, because Manual deliberately shows no object to brush. Split, the brush serves both modes, the object gets a whole canvas, and a user whose PNG arrived already cut out just presses Next. brief.md § The shape carries the three-stage table.

Stage 2 is skippable BY CONSTRUCTION, no flag: with no cut and no stroke its STEP_MEDIA adapter returns null, and the frame treats a null as 'this kind changed nothing', so image2 reaches the run exactly as supplied.

Stage 3 cannot see stage 2 through `sourceRole` alone - _buildStepSlide resolves media from _mediaGroups (the user's inputs) while stage 2's file is derived at Run. The seam is `sourceValue`, one line: MpiStepPlace then composes the object from bgUrl + userMask, which is the shape composePlacedObject already takes. Do NOT persist a derived file instead - that re-cuts an already-cut picture on every Reuse.

TWO MASK LAYERS, NEVER FLATTENED. Flatten bgMask into userMask and toggling Remove Background off destroys every erasure. Keeping them apart is also what makes the brush work with the toggle OFF (the base alpha becomes the object's own rectangle) and what makes toggling free in both directions.
The composite runs against the ORIGINAL RGB, never the cut-out's, so Restore reveals real pixels. A cut-out PNG's colour under alpha 0 is encoder-dependent (memory tools/image-alpha-flatten.md).
